correctness.rationale: Every one of the 25 finite complexes is exhaustively enumerated. The attached source verifies matching disjointness and 5,376 directed Hasse incidences by topological sorts; a Morse CW complex with only one 0-cell and r 2-cells is the wedge of r 2-spheres, similarly for 1-sphere links. Elementary simplicial free-face collapses are independently checked for all four remaining links, and their contractibility gives homotopy invariance of the deletion inclusions by the cone decomposition. The alternate LCF presentation independently confirms mod-two boundary ranks and vertex correspondence. All statements are restricted to the explicit 12-vertex graph and its 12 deletions/links.

originality.rationale: Distinct complete Frucht-graph vertex-deletion/link homotopy classification, proved by exhaustive discrete-Morse certificates. Barmak gives only suspension under a triangle-free-vertex hypothesis that applies here, not exact wedge multiplicities or links. Targeted literature-index and primary-paper searches did not identify an equivalent or stronger covering theorem; residual unindexed-literature risk remains.
residual_risks: An unpublished or unindexed computation could reproduce some or all of the per-vertex classification; a negative search is not novelty proof.

value.rationale: The Frucht graph is a canonical smallest cubic asymmetric graph: no nontrivial automorphisms exist to identify its twelve vertex deletions. The exact 3-way homotopy landscape detects four deletion-invariant vertices, six reducing the second Betti rank, and two increasing it. This is a natural complete classification rather than a relabeling or isolated low-complexity check; the links identify the topological mechanism of each regime. Its exact integral wedge results and collapsible links are not implied by generic suspension results or graph-adjacency data.
